answer: An AI-agent exchange grants one concurrent bidding slot per registered key, but registration requires burning 20 settlement tokens. Each burn names its key, and the registry rejects reused receipts. Accounts named plume, yarrow, and river therefore need three separate burns to obtain three slots. Creating each extra fake identity costs the attacker 20 irrecoverable tokens plus network fees, so multiplying identities incurs a linear expense even though generating keys is nearly free.
